Subject: Post-call: Reserved GPU + isolation plan for SynTex — next steps

Hi Eleanor — thanks again for carving out time earlier. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we loop in procurement and infra: 

Summary of what we heard (pain & goals)
- Latency unpredictability during traffic spikes is affecting product SLAs (goal: p95 < 300ms for inference).
- Need strict tenant isolation for PHI workloads; SynTex must ensure no cross-tenant data leakage.
- Expected steady-state throughput ~200 req/s, with bursts up to ~1k req/s for short workloads (1–5 min).
- Must support model variants (internal model + open LLM) and ability to pin versions for audits.
- Compliance ask: SOC 2 evidence, KMS integration for keys, audit logs retained 12 months.

Redwood proposal (high level)
- Dedicated (reserved) GPU pool: isolated tenant pool with VPC peering and dedicated nodes. We recommend starting with a 6-GPU reserved pool (H100-equivalent) with horizontal burst capacity to handle short spikes.
- Isolation model: tenant-silo (dedicated pool) + optional node-level encryption + KMS/HSM integration.
- SLOs: target 99.9% uptime SLA for reserved pool; latency SLOs configurable per-route — we can aim for p95 <300ms for your standard model under the proposed sizing.
- Cost controls: burst policies, autoscale caps, and prefix/KV caching to reduce per-token cost while satisfying latency.

Next steps we proposed on the call
1) I’ll send a short pricing estimate and an ops playbook (attached).
2) Ben will follow up with a short technical note on model/quantization tradeoffs that affect GPU sizing.
3) SynTex to confirm procurement timeline and whether a PO or contract amendment is preferred.
4) Schedule a technical deep-dive (30–45m) to validate network/VPC details and sticky session behavior.

Questions for you (please reply inline)
- Is a 6-GPU reserved starting point reasonable, or should we size higher to cover peak SLA headroom?
- Who should be on the procurement thread (legal/procurement contact)?
- Do you have any hard constraints on retention/encryption beyond SOC 2 / 12 months?

Attachments: call-recording-20260823.mp3 (audio), SynTex-Security-Overview.pdf (you shared during the call)

Thanks — happy to iterate. Proposed deep-dive: Mon, Aug 31 at 10:00 AM PT — does that work?

Eleanor / Neha — quick follow-up on technical sizing and burst behavior. Thanks for the call. A few points to consider that will impact committed size and pricing: 

- Model footprint: if you plan to run a 30–40B parameter model (quantized to q4/q8), per-inference memory and latency change substantially versus a 13B variant. If SynTex expects to use a mix, we recommend reserving capacity based on the heaviest profile you want to meet SLOs for.

- Suggested baseline: 6 x H100-equivalent GPUs (reserved pool) with configuration to pin the pool to SynTex (tenant-silo). This gives predictable p95 latency for heavier models.

- Burst design: burst capacity is implemented via a warm standby lane — the system keeps a small number of nodes in a warm state (pre-warmed KV cache and model loaded) to reduce cold-start spikes. Typical warmup to full capacity ~60–120s depending on model size and sequence length. We can pre-warm during scheduled windows.

- Caching: recommend prefix/KV caching on hot routes (results in 30–60% cost reduction for repeated prompts).

- Compliance/ops: logs exported to an S3 bucket in your preferred AWS region; we can provide an export bundle for auditors and an API for log pulls. KMS integration supported via your AWS KMS — we can sign an addendum if HSM is required.

I attached our isolation ops playbook and a short sizing spreadsheet (pricing estimate to follow from Neha).

Attachments: isolation-ops-playbook.pdf

-ben
